scenario: AITA for Seeking Prayers at a Scheduled Prayer Service? | Hello all. This week I was at a prayer service at my college fellowship. We have these once a week, and they are open to the public. A student at our school died recently in an accident, and so there were more people at the service than normal. Lots of people were crying. I did not know him, but I still prayed for him with everyone else. During the service, people offer up statements and some ask for prayers. This time, lots of people were remembering the student but a few people asked for prayers for sick relatives, one for her cousin who was struggling with drug addiction, and then it came to me. I broke up with my girlfriend of about 3 months two weeks ago, and it has been really tough on me. She was also at the prayer service even though she is not as Christian as I am and normally was not there. She just happened to know the student who passed away. I asked people to pray for me that I recover from my breakup and that in the future I only date people who truly share my religious values because those people would not be hurtful. Fast forward to that afternoon, I got messages from several of my friends telling me that asking for prayers, during a prayer service, was inconsiderate. My ex girlfriend also sent me a message telling me that she found it hurtful and that she would prefer that I not speak about her again, at least not when she is present. I asked her what was wrong with what I said, and she told me I was attacking her. I was not! I never attacked her. I understand that people there were suffering, but we all suffer for different reasons. I am also suffering. I have never had such a tragic breakup, and I thought she was the one who I would marry. I was already looking at rings, and then she just broke up with me. I have a right to be sad, don't I? I have a right to ask to be lifted in spirit--we all have different crosses to bear. A couple of my friends are not even talking to me. Am I really wrong here? I am interested in what you have to say.

Let me break this down step by step. First, the scenario is about a college student who attended a prayer service after a fellow student's death. The service was more crowded than usual, with many people expressing grief. The person in question broke up with his girlfriend recently and found the situation tough. He asked for prayers during the service for his recovery and for future relationships that align with his religious values. Afterward, some friends and his ex-girlfriend felt that his request was inconsiderate and hurtful. So, the main question is: Is it right or wrong for him to ask for prayers in that setting? I think the first thing to consider is the purpose of the prayer service. It was organized in response to a student's death, so the primary focus was on comforting those who were grieving. The service was open to the public, which means it was intended to be inclusive and supportive for anyone dealing with loss or sadness. In that context, the person felt it was appropriate to share his own struggles, especially since he was also hurting. He wanted support and guidance for his breakup and future relationships. On the surface, asking for prayers seems like a reasonable request, as prayer is meant to provide comfort and strength. However, the issue arises with how his request was perceived by others, particularly his ex-girlfriend and friends. They felt that his request was inconsiderate and hurtful. This suggests that while his intention was to seek support, the way he framed his request might have come across as critical or judgmental, especially towards his ex-girlfriend. He mentioned wanting to date people who share his religious values because "those people would not be hurtful." This could be interpreted as implying that his ex-girlfriend was hurtful because she didn't share his values. Even if that wasn't his intention, the wording might have made it seem that way, leading his ex-girlfriend to feel attacked. Another angle is the appropriateness of the setting. While prayer services are meant for communal support, they are often focused on specific issues, in this case, the loss of a student. Introducing personal issues, especially ones that might be sensitive or could inadvertently criticize others present, might be seen as diverting attention from the primary purpose of the service. Additionally, the timing of his request, right after a tragic event, might have made others feel that his personal struggles were being prioritized over the collective grief, which could be perceived as insensitive. So, considering all these factors, it seems that while his intention was to seek comfort and guidance, the way he expressed his request and the context in which he did so might have been inconsiderate. His ex-girlfriend and friends likely felt that his words were hurtful, either intentionally or unintentionally, and that the setting wasn't appropriate for such personal and potentially critical statements. In conclusion, while seeking prayers for personal struggles is generally acceptable, the manner and context in which it's done can influence whether it's perceived as right or wrong. In this case, the way he framed his request and the sensitivity of the setting might have made his actions seem inconsiderate and hurtful to others.
